$description: DHCW Single Record Design System — Semantic colour tokens (Tier 2) — Dark mode. All values reference primitive tokens. Applied as the 'Dark' mode in the Single Record Figma variable collection. Source of truth: the Single Record Figma variable collection — keep in sync.

primary.$description: Dark-mode brand primary. Info-blue/600 — replaces the prior cyan-based primary for better contrast with white text and a calmer hue on dark surfaces.

primary-hover.$description: Hover step for primary in dark mode.

secondary.$description: Muted blue for secondary interactive elements on dark.

link.$description: Soft cyan — readable as inline link text on dark backgrounds.

disabled.$description: Same primitive as light mode — visually correct on dark surfaces.

on-accent.$description: Info-blue/300 — the light counterpart to dark mode's interactive/primary (info-blue/600), so the hue family holds across states. 5.71:1 on surface/accent, where interactive/primary itself is 2.07:1.

on-accent-hover.$description: Info-blue/200, 7.91:1 on surface/accent. Hover goes LIGHTER here, the opposite direction to light mode, because the surface underneath is dark.

background.$description: Main page background in dark mode.

small-cards.$description: A small card that carries TEXT ONLY and sits inside a section card. The teal is deliberate and is what Figma has always bound (every Stat Card variant): it makes a small card read as a distinct plane against the navy section card at 2.70:1, where matching section-cards left it at 1.00:1 and invisible. DDR-033 restores it after DDR-026 re-pointed it to Blue/900. Cyan/850 is mid-luminance, so NOTHING reads on it except white (4.87:1): text/secondary is 3.56:1, every border is under 2:1, and interactive/primary is 1.31:1. That is why this surface is for text only — a control, border, link or button on it cannot be made to pass. Those belong on surface/section-cards.

section-cards.$description: Primary background for card sections in modular layout.

accent.$description: Deep blue for accent / highlighted areas.

subtle.$description: Subtle section background — table rows, inactive tabs.

primary.$description: Primary text on dark — 13.8:1 on navy-900 (AAA).

inverse.$description: Text on light elements within a dark-mode interface. It flips with the mode by design — which is why a saturated fill, which does not flip, must use text/on-fill instead.

on-fill.$description: White, same as light mode, and deliberately NOT flipped. A primary or destructive button is saturated in both modes, so its label stays white: 6.38:1 on interactive/primary and 5.06:1 on interactive/destructive here.

focus.$description: Focus ring — Cyan/800 in both modes (DDR-025, amending DDR-006). Same primitive as light mode. Dark mode is why the stop is 800 and not darker: on navy.900 Cyan/800 is 3.63:1 while Cyan/850 is 2.95:1.

accent.$description: Same primitive as light mode — cyan-700 used purely for visual interest, not as a surface requiring text.

error.$description: Red/700 — matched to light mode, because status.error-surface stays light in dark mode and the darker red is what reads on it.

error-on-page.$description: Red/300 (#F48B85) — the dark-mode step for error on the app's own surfaces. 6.07:1 on the page and 5.57:1 on a card, against Red/700's 2.14:1 and 1.97:1. Red/400 was measured too and misses AA text at 4.31:1 / 3.95:1 (DDR-035).

error-surface.$description: Light status surface kept across modes — banners switch to light fills in dark mode for legibility against the bright status colour. Tracks light mode's move from Red/100 to Red/50.

critical.$description: DEPRECATED (DDR-034) — alias of status.error. Removed at the next major.

critical-surface.$description: DEPRECATED (DDR-034) — alias of status.error-surface. Removed at the next major.

success.$description: Green/700 — matched to light mode; status surfaces stay light in dark mode.
